tagline: Old brick and back roads around Bunnell, three centuries in use.
intro: The roads fan out from Bunnell, the Flagler County seat. SR 100 runs eight miles east to Flagler Beach, SR 11 runs southwest past the preserve land around Codys Corner, US 1 crosses through town, and county roads lead out to Espanola, where the Old Brick Road begins. Some 98 miles in all, in Flagler, St. Johns and Volusia counties.

Native tribes, European conquerors, colonists and pre-interstate tourists have all used this network over some 300 years. Bunnell itself is named for Alvah A. Bunnell, a shingle maker who supplied wood to the young railroads.

moments.title: Espanola
moments.text: Here starts the Old Brick Road, one of the few stretches of the original brick Dixie Highway left in Florida, still open to walkers, bicycles and cars.

moments.title: Bulow Plantation Ruins Historic State Park
moments.text: West of Flagler Beach stand the coquina ruins of the sugar mill of East Florida's largest plantation, worked by enslaved people, visited by Audubon, and destroyed in the Seminole War of 1836.

moments.title: Codys Corner
moments.text: A crossroads named in 1907 by a farmer, Richard Cody, and known by the 1950s for its artesian irrigation wells.
